title.narrative: Akuta energibehov i Ukraina 2024-2026: UNDP:s program för grön energiomställning
Emergency Response to Urgent Energy Needs in Ukraine

description.narrative: Det föreslagna stödet förväntas bidra till att upphandla, leverera och installera elverk och kraftgeneratorer, samt annan utrustning för att göra det möjligt för staden Charkiv att tillhandahålla el, värme, rent vatten och sanitetstjänster till 1,3 miljoner invånare, inklusive över 350 000 internflyktingar. Stöd till Charkiv är prioriterat i insatsen då kapaciteten för energiförsörjning är kraftigt nedsatt av de omfattande ryska attackerna i mars och april 2024, men även andra stora städer kan bli aktuella utifrån UNDP:s bedömningar av sårbarheten för energiförsörjningen.

The proposed intervention is expected to contribute to procurement, delivery and installation of electric power and combined heat and power generators, as well as other equipment to enable the city of Kharkiv to provide electricity, heat, clean water and sanitation services to 1.3 million residents, including over 350,000 internally displaced persons. The intervention will target Kharkiv as the first priority, where energy supply was severely damaged by Russian strikes in March and April 2024, but also other major population centers, as per the assessment of vulnerability of energy supply performed by UNDP.

title.narrative: Agreement Emergency Response to Urgent Energy Needs in Ukraine
Decision Emergency Response to Urgent Energy Needs in Ukraine

description.narrative:
Under Outcome 1
In 2024, Sida's contribution funded procurement of 4 gas-piston cogeneration units (with capacity of 1.5 megawatts (MW) each) and 2 gas-piston cogeneration units (3.3 MW each) for the city of Kharkiv. This was part of a larger procurement of 10 units to provide back up power to Kharkiv Heating Networks, a municipal enterprise operating the city distric heating system. By December 2024, 6 out of 10 units were delivered, with the remaining 4 scheduled for delivery by May 2025. The comissioning was scheduled for mid-2025.
In November 2024, UNDP signed a contract for 12.9 MW gas turbine for the Kyiv region. The procurement was to be funded with the contribution from Sida and the Mininstry of Foreign Affairs of Sweden. The turbine would cover 6% of back up power needs for Kyiv region's critical infrastructure, benefiting enstimated 105,000 people in Kyiv region.
UNDP with the support of the Mininstry of Foreign Affairs of Sweden procured a 2.5 MW gas piston generator to assist with the energy recovery efforts in Zaporizhzhia. This is part of a broader initiative to procure 8 gas-piston gensets, collectively providing a total capacity of 19.4 MW. The remaining 7 units are financed by the Government of Denmark (3 units), the Government of Belgium (2 units), and the European Commission, through the UNDP project Crisis Response for Securing Reliable Energy Access in Ukraine (FPI Energy) (2 units).
The report also mentions procurement and delivery of energy equipment financed with contributions from the Swedish As such in 2024, UNDP procured a 3.3 MW gas-fired piston genset to bolster energy resilience in Odesa. This initiative was part of a broader effort involving procurement and delivery of 6 gas-fired piston gensets, with a total capacity of 19.8 MW. The remaining 5 units were funded by the Government of Norway (1 unit) and the Government of Japan (4 units).
With funding from the MFA, UNDP procured a 330/110kV 195MVA autotransformer for Ukrenergo substation. High-power autotransformers are critical components of power substations, regulating voltage levels in electricity transmission networks. It is estimated that the capacity of this transformer would enable access to electricity for up to 1,800,000 people, strengthening grid stability and ensuring reliable power distribution across the region.
Under Outcome 2
With expert support from UNDPs Green Energy Recovery Programme and funding from Sweden and NORAD, draft law No. 9381 was developed to simplify regulations and boost investment in Ukraine's decentralized, sustainable energy sector. It streamlines grid connections, enables cable pooling, and improves investment conditions, accelerating projects, strengthening investor confidence, and enhancing energy security, especially in crisis situations.
UNDP also provided legal expertise for the draft Law On the Principles of Green Reconstruction, aligning it with international commitments like the Paris Agreement and the European Green Deal. Supported by Sweden and NORAD, this work included analyzing existing legislation and embedding sustainability principles into Ukraines reconstruction framework.
